question.problem:
The dimensions of a stamp are $2.1\,\text{cm}\times 2.4\,\text{cm}$, where each dimension is measured to the nearest $0.1\,\text{cm}.$ Rounded to the nearest tenth of a square centimeter, what is the upper bound for the area of the stamp?

To the nearest tenth of a square centimeter, the upper bound is
{{field-1}}${\text{cm}}^{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
Each dimension is given to the nearest $0.1\,\text{cm}.$ So, the greatest possible error of these measurements is

$$
\frac{0.1\,\text{cm}}{2}=0.05\,\text{cm}.
$$

We wish to find the *upper bound* for the area of the stamp. Therefore, we require the *upper bound* of each dimension.

The upper bounds for each dimension are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & 2.1\,\text{cm}+0.05\,\text{cm}=2.15\,\text{cm} \\  & 2.4\,\text{cm}+0.05\,\text{cm}=2.45\,\text{cm}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the upper bound for the area of the stamp is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =2.15\,\text{cm}\times 2.45\,\text{cm} \\  & =5.267\,5\,{\text{cm}}^{2} \\  & ≈5.3\,{\text{cm}}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest tenth of a square centimeter.
